Tamil Nadu School Closures Declared in Several Districts Amid Heavy Rainfall

28 Oct 2026, 08:49 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Education Desk · Source: timesofindia.indiatimes.com

Image: timesofindia.indiatimes.com — Creative Commons

Key takeaways District-Wise School Closures and Status School administrations in multiple districts of Tamil Nadu declared closures following heavy rainfall across parts of the state. According to reports, educational institutions in Tirunelveli, Thoothukudi, Kanniyakumari, Tenkasi

District-Wise School Closures and Status

School administrations in multiple districts of Tamil Nadu declared closures following heavy rainfall across parts of the state. According to reports, educational institutions in Tirunelveli, Thoothukudi, Kanniyakumari, Tenkasi, and Tirupattur are shut as local authorities monitor weather conditions, waterlogging risks, and potential flooding.

In contrast, schools in Chennai, Tiruvallur, Kancheepuram, and Chengalpattu remain open. While these northern districts experienced closures on the preceding day due to intense downpours, authorities have not extended the holiday.

Rainfall Distribution and Meteorological Forecast

Recent weather spells brought substantial precipitation to various regions. MGR Nagar recorded 15 cm of rainfall, while Mamallapuram registered 9 cm. In southern districts, Tenkasi and Sattankulam in Thoothukudi each recorded 6 cm, and Tirunelveli saw 5 cm.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast continued rainfall throughout the state, driven by a low-pressure area over the southwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining coastal regions. Isolated locations face the possibility of heavy to very heavy showers, accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning. An orange alert remains in effect for southern areas, where precipitation could reach up to 20 cm in certain spots.

Practical Implications and Verification

Heavy rainfall has heightened concerns regarding transport disruptions and waterlogging in vulnerable areas. Residents living in low-lying neighborhoods or near riverbanks are advised to adhere to local safety advisories and avoid flooded roads.

Because holiday declarations are managed at the local level and weather alerts do not automatically trigger closures, families must verify updates directly.

Readers can check official announcements and verify the original report through the [Times of India Education News](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/education/news/tamil-nadu-school-holiday-today-schools-closed-in-several-districts-amid-heavy-rainfall-check-details-here/articleshow/135105471.cms).
